clue.text: Prohibition has young hooligan stuck in outhouse

parts.note: a bar is a ban or prohibition
a ned is a young Scottish hooligan

explanation.surface: A ban on alcohol leaves a teenage tearaway shut away in a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuck in outhouse' looks like part of the story, but it is the definition: to barn something is to store it in a barn.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb barn means to store in a barn, so barned describes something put away in that farm building.

clue.text: Plant with insect gathering prime bit of nectar repeatedly

indicators.note: something gathering other things collects them inside itself

parts.note: a bee is an insect; it is split around the inner letters

indicators.note: the prime bit of a word is its opening letter, the first one written

parts.note: the first letter of nectar, taken twice

explanation.surface: A plant visited by a bee that keeps sipping its nectar.
explanation.definitionFit: Benne is another name for sesame, an oil-seed plant, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: A container, yours, decorated with a prickly plant

parts.note: taken as written
a can is a container
thine is the old form of yours

explanation.surface: Someone's pot has been ornamented with a spiky plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Acanthine describes ornament in the style of acanthus leaves, as on Corinthian capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthine means like or ornamented with the acanthus, a spiny-leaved plant used as a decorative motif.

clue.text: Limited number with a skill in the time of the Flood

definitions.text: in the time of the Flood

parts.note: No. is the shortened form of number
taken as written
Chambers gives chic as artistic skill as well as style

explanation.surface: Only a few people had the craft needed when the waters rose.
explanation.definitionFit: Noachic means relating to Noah or his era, and Noah's era is that of the biblical Flood.

clue.text: Jock's occasional place of retreat with interior design

indicators.note: a word with an interior has something else filling its middle

parts.note: a den is a private retreat
a design is an aim or intention

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's occasional bolthole has a designer interior.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a nickname for a Scot, so 'Jock's' marks a Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: Daimen is the Scots adjective for occasional or rare, as in Burns's 'a daimen icker'.

clue.text: Gift to hospital — holy book

parts.note: a grant is a gift of money
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A charitable donation to a hospital includes a sacred text.
explanation.definitionFit: The Granth, or Guru Granth Sahib, is the sacred scripture of Sikhism.

clue.text: Being received inadequately, weep as of old

indicators.note: done inadequately means not finished, so the last letter is missing

parts.note: being received is being greeted

explanation.surface: Getting a poor welcome makes someone cry, in old-fashioned language.
explanation.definitionFit: Greete is a Spenserian spelling of greet, an old and Scots verb meaning to weep or cry.

clue.text: When a river makes more than one bank

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A river produces several banks along its course.
explanation.walkthrough: Asar is the plural of as, a long glacial ridge of gravel, also called an esker.
explanation.definitionFit: An as is a ridge or bank of glacial gravel, and asar is its plural, so it names several such banks.

clue.text: Antelope, one seen in Netherlands and part of Germany once

indicators.note: a thing seen in a place is located within it

parts.note: NL is the international code for the Netherlands
the Roman numeral for one
a Gau was a political district of Germany, especially under the Nazis

explanation.surface: An antelope spotted in the Low Countries and a corner of old Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The nilgau, or nilgai, is a large Indian antelope, the blue bull.

clue.text: Shrub no longer easy for the female to accommodate

indicators.note: to accommodate a guest is to take them in, so these letters house others

parts.note: her is the female pronoun; it goes around the other piece
eath is an obsolete word for easy

explanation.surface: A bush that a woman finds harder to fit into her garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather is a low evergreen shrub of moorland, also called ling.

clue.text: Flea perhaps coming to grief in Erica's teapot

indicators.note: something coming to grief is wrecked, so its letters end up in disorder

parts.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A flea has fallen into Erica's teapot and met its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea lives on the outside of its host, which makes it an example of an external parasite.

clue.text: Nocturnal animal may be food to a snake

parts.note: a naga is a snake, especially a cobra or serpent deity in Hindu myth
a pie is food

explanation.surface: A night creature could end up as a serpent's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The food is added to the snake, so it comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The nagapie is the South African name for the bushbaby, a small primate active at night.

clue.text: Hunger after salmon in a traditional Scottish dish

indicators.note: one thing placed after another is written following it

parts.note: a parr is a young salmon
an itch is a hunger or craving

explanation.surface: A craving for salmon sits within a classic Scottish meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Parritch is the Scots form of porridge, the traditional oatmeal breakfast of Scotland.

clue.text: Chance going round avenue you'll see insect captured

indicators.note: a word going round another encircles it, sitting either side

parts.note: slant is informal for a chance or opportunity
Ave is the abbreviation for avenue

explanation.surface: If you happen to walk round the avenue you'll spot a caught bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A slave ant is an ant captured as a pupa by slave-making ants and raised to work for them.

clue.text: Leading Greek character said to be a grass

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: The first letter of the Greek alphabet is reputed to be a type of grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfa is another name for esparto, a tough North African grass used in papermaking.

clue.text: Maybe an old bird perches finally on beast of burden

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing on another sits in front of it
finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of perches
a camel is a pack animal

explanation.surface: Perhaps a bird of long ago comes to roost at last on a camel.
explanation.walkthrough: Scamel appears once in Shakespeare's Tempest; nobody is sure what it is, perhaps a bird, hence 'Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors guess Shakespeare's scamel was a seabird such as a godwit, so it may be an archaic bird name.

clue.text: Plant I found in cave here unexpectedly

indicators.note: things turning up unexpectedly are out of their expected order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone surprised to discover a plant growing in this cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Echeveria is a genus of rosette-forming succulent plants from Central America.

clue.text: Creature from outer space children design

parts.note: ET is the film's extra-terrestrial
ch. is the abbreviation for children

explanation.surface: An alien makes a drawing for the kids.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut a design into metal or glass, so as a verb it means to design by engraving.

clue.text: Scripture that may be rendered in a chant

indicators.note: a piece rendered is rearranged or translated into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Holy writ that a choir might sing in plainsong.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tanach is the Hebrew Bible, the Jewish scriptures of Law, Prophets and Writings.

clue.text: Dung and fibre kept in tin

indicators.note: something kept in a vessel is stored inside it

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin; it goes around the other piece
a hair is a fibre

explanation.surface: Manure and roughage being stored in a can.
explanation.definitionFit: Shairn is a Scots word for dung, especially cow dung.

clue.text: Old deer springs, keeping time, jumping up

indicators.note: something keeping an item holds it inside

parts.note: spas are mineral springs; they go around the other piece

indicators.note: in a down entry jumping up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: Elderly stags leap up from springs, keeping to their schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A spayad is an obsolete term for a male red deer in its third year, so spayads are old deer.

clue.text: Material old-fashioned company's given to poor actor

parts.note: ging is an obsolete word for a company or gang
a ham is an overacting performer

explanation.surface: Fabric that an antiquated troupe hands to a bad actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingham is a checked or striped cotton cloth, so it is a type of material.

clue.text: This unfortunate woman, getting red, is harangued terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are jumbled
the answer getting a word added makes up the longer word, so that word must be taken back out

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A wretched woman is flushed after being berated harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a subtractive anagram: the answer plus RED is an anagram of HARANGUED, so take RED out of HARANGUED and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish law an agunah is a woman whose husband has vanished or refuses a divorce, leaving her unable to remarry.

clue.text: Heartless bloke to show great anger spinning round

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of the word has been removed

parts.note: a guy is a bloke
to rant is to rave angrily

explanation.surface: A callous man flies into a rage and starts to whirl.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyrant is an adjective meaning gyrating, so it describes something rotating or whirling.

clue.text: Robber making return, getting cut short, one captured

indicators.note: something captured is held inside another thing
a word cut short has lost its final letter

parts.note: to revert is to return to a former state
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A thief comes back, is stopped short, and one of the gang is caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A reiver is a raider or plunderer, especially of the Anglo-Scottish border country, so a robber.

clue.text: Unruly sort around island behaves rowdily

indicators.note: one thing set around another surrounds it
unruly means disorderly, so these letters are not in their proper order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged; the result goes around the island
Is. is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A wild type of person on an island acts like a hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: To roist, like roister, means to bluster or carouse noisily.

clue.text: Anxious and cross when one deemed good displaces king

indicators.note: displaces means pushes something out and takes its place

parts.note: cross means angry
a saint is considered good; St is its abbreviation
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king; it is swapped out

explanation.surface: Someone is worried and annoyed when a saintly figure dethrones the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Angsty is an informal adjective for full of angst, meaning anxious or troubled.

clue.text: Snow yet to return

parts.note: even means yet, as in 'even more'

explanation.surface: The snow has not yet come back.
explanation.definitionFit: Névé is the granular compacted snow at the top of a glacier, so it is a kind of snow.

clue.text: Sheep on street close by in Scotland

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A sheep standing in the road near a Scottish croft.

clue.text: After a brief time duck becomes dry

clue.text: Show fear, weeping — no yen, little energy

E is the symbol for energy

clue.text: Senior not all trainees wanted

clue.text: Darling husband taken into a shop

H is the abbreviation for husband

clue.text: Troubled ass — indicator reveals disease caused by worms

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Municipal officer beginning to cheer in call for round of drinks

parts.note: the first letter of cheer

clue.text: Something that cat sat on tot sits on

the nursery rhyme line 'the cat sat on the mat'
